ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All individuals and legal entities identified as beneficial owners at or above the 25% threshold must be screened before incorporation and continuously thereafter against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, Taiwan's domestic terrorism financing list under the Counter-Terrorism Financing Act, and China's Sanctions and Implementation List. Screening must include fuzzy matching, aliases and name variants, PEP status verification against Taiwan and international PEP databases, adverse negative media checks, and periodic rescreening every 30 days. Any PEP or sanctions alert requires enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and documented risk mitigation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Department of Commerce - Company and Business Name Pre-Approval System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names in Taiwan must be in Traditional Chinese characters. The statutory naming convention requires a four-tier structure: (1) a distinct trade name; (2) a business scope description; (3) an organizational form label such as Limited, Company, or Limited by Shares; and (4) any trademark or distinctive identifier. Foreign names are permitted transliterations but must not create confusion with existing registered names. The name must accurately reflect the registered business scope and cannot mislead as to the nature of the entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of receiving the rejection notice, under the Taiwan Administrative Appeal Act. The appeal must cite the statutory grounds, include the original rejection notice, the proposed name, business scope, and supporting documentation showing that the name does not conflict or mislead. MOEA must render a decision within three months; if rejected again, the applicant may bring an administrative action in the Taipei High Administrative Court within 30 days. Concurrently, the applicant may immediately submit a revised name application without forfeiting priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a PropTech SaaS entity classified under ISIC 6201 and NAICS 531390, Taiwan's Company Act requires a legally valid registered office address within Taiwan. Virtual offices provided by licensed commercial registration service providers are permissible for company registration in most municipalities, but they are subject to rejection by the National Taxation Bureau and corporate banks if the address is used solely as a commercial mailbox without a lease agreement, telephone lines, staff, or business records. Because the company's ancillary activity of real estate property screening may be regarded as property management, MOEA and municipal tax authorities will likely require verifiable physical substance. A physical administrative office with a signed lease and operational infrastructure is recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood of unannounced inspection is Medium, estimated at 25% annual probability for a low-risk SaaS business, rising to 45% if only a virtual office is declared. Physical inspection checklist: (1) staff presence during business hours; (2) lease agreement in the company's name; (3) active power, internet, and telephone services; (4) company signboard or building directory entry; (5) VAT and payroll records; (6) service contracts and invoices; (7) server or cloud infrastructure documentation; (8) bank statements showing running operating expenses.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), Articles 1-10, 128-156, 172-180, 208-210, 387-388, and 393-394; Foreign Investment Act, Articles 1-12; Business Registration Act, Articles 1-8
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Central Company Registration Office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation and Application for Company Registration (Form 1) filed with the MOEA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Taiwan law does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for limited companies; however, the subscribed capital must be fully paid in cash or in-kind as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, and the initial capital must be deposited in a temporary escrow account at a domestic bank until the company is registered, after which the funds are released to the company's operating account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (the 'Company'), a company incorporated under the laws of the Republic of China (Taiwan), held at [Registered Office Address] on [Date] at [Time]. PRESENT: All directors of the Company, namely [Director A], [Director B], and [Director C], constituting a quorum. The Chairman, [Director A], presided over the meeting. The following resolutions were duly proposed, seconded, and unanimously adopted: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT: RESOLVED, that the Company's authorized share capital is NT$[Amount] divided into [Number] ordinary shares of NT$[Par Value] each, and that the initial subscribed capital of NT$[Amount] (the 'Initial Capital') be allotted to the shareholders as set forth in the Subscription Schedule attached hereto. The Board acknowledges receipt of the full consideration for the Initial Capital, which has been deposited into the Company's temporary escrow account at [Bank Name] under account number [Account Number], and directs the Chief Financial Officer to transfer such funds to the Company's operating account upon issuance of the Company's registration certificate. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Company shall open and maintain a corporate bank account with [Bank Name] (the 'Bank'), and that the Chairman, the Chief Executive Officer, and the Chief Financial Officer, each acting singly, are hereby authorized to sign, execute, and deliver all documents, agreements, and instruments necessary to open, operate, and manage the Bank Account, including but not limited to deposit agreements, wire transfer instructions, and loan documents, subject to the Company's internal approval thresholds. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [Full Address], Taiwan, and that the Company shall maintain its statutory records, corporate seal, and minute books at such address. The Board authorizes the Company Secretary to file all necessary notices and amendments with the Ministry of Economic Affairs regarding the registered office. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed to the offices indicated, each to serve until their successors are duly elected and qualified: (a) [Director A] as Chairman of the Board and Managing Director; (b) [Director B] as Chief Executive Officer; (c) [Director C] as Chief Financial Officer; and (d) [Name] as Company Secretary. Each officer shall have the powers and duties as prescribed by the Company Act, the Articles of Incorporation, and the Board's delegation of authority. 5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to take all actions necessary to effectuate the foregoing resolutions, including the preparation and filing of all statutory forms, payment of all fees, and engagement of professional advisors. This resolution shall be effective immediately and shall be recorded in the minutes of this meeting. The meeting was adjourned at [Time]. Certified by: [Company Secretary]

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Company Name Reservation Online System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for company name reservation via the MOEA's online portal. The proposed name must not conflict with existing registered names or trademarks. Provide the intended business scope (ISIC 6201 - Computer programming activities) and the proposed English and Chinese names (if any). The application must be signed by the proposed incorporator or a notarized power of attorney. After approval, the name reservation is valid for six months. Simultaneously, if foreign investment is involved, file a pre-approval application with the Investment Commission of the MOEA under the Foreign Investment Act.
required_dossiers: Copy of passport or ID of incorporators
Foreign investment pre-approval application (if foreign shareholders)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, file an appeal with the MOEA within 15 days, providing evidence of distinctiveness or a revised name. If the foreign investment pre-approval is queried, submit additional documentation on the source of funds and beneficial ownership within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public and MOEA (for later filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Taiwan-licensed attorney to draft the Articles of Incorporation in compliance with the Company Act. The Articles must include the company name, business scope, registered office address, share capital structure, classes of shares, rights of shareholders, board composition, and quorum requirements. All incorporators must sign the Articles, and the signatures must be notarized by a Taiwan notary public. If any incorporator is a foreign entity, the signature must be authenticated by the Taiwan representative office in the foreign jurisdiction or by apostille. The notarized Articles are then submitted to the MOEA as part of the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Notarized identification documents of all incorporators
Proof of address for registered office (lease agreement or title deed)
Power of attorney for the attorney-in-fact
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA returns the Articles for correction, the attorney must amend and re-notarize the document within 14 days. If the notarization is challenged, obtain a court order or re-execute the signatures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Bank (e.g., Bank of Taiwan, Cathay United Bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the name of the company to be formed. Deposit the initial paid-up capital as stated in the Articles. The bank will issue a capital deposit certificate, which is a mandatory document for registration. After the company is registered, the funds are transferred to the company's permanent operating account. The bank must verify the identity of all signatories and the source of funds. For foreign shareholders, the funds must be remitted through foreign exchange procedures and reported to the Central Bank of China (Taiwan).
required_dossiers: Passport/ID copies of directors and shareholders
Proof of source of funds (e.g., bank statements)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the deposit due to anti-money laundering concerns, provide additional beneficial ownership declarations and source of wealth documentation. If the foreign exchange remittance is delayed, obtain a temporary approval from the Central Bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Central Company Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation application package to the MOEA, including the notarized Articles, capital deposit certificate, name reservation certificate, foreign investment approval (if any), and the application form. The MOEA will review the documents for compliance with the Company Act. Upon approval, the MOEA issues a Company Registration Certificate and assigns a unified business number. This registration is the legal birth of the company. The entire process can be done online via the MOEA's Company Registration and Administration System.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOEA issues a deficiency notice, the applicant has 30 days to cure the defects. If the application is rejected, the applicant may appeal to the Administrative Appeals Commission within 30 days. If the rejection is due to a legal defect, the applicant must amend the Articles and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance) and Local Municipal Government
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Company Registration Certificate, register for tax purposes with the National Taxation Bureau. Obtain a Business Registration Certificate from the local municipal government (if required for the business address). Apply for a tax identification number (TIN) and register for VAT and corporate income tax. If the company will employ staff, register with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration. For a SaaS company, no special industry license is required, but if the company processes personal data, it must comply with the Personal Data Protection Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is delayed, the company may be subject to penalties. If the business registration is queried, provide additional proof of the physical office address. If the company fails to register for labor insurance, it may face fines; cure by immediate registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Finance, Taxation Agency; operational competence is delegated to the five National Taxation Bureaus (e.g., National Taxation Bureau of Taipei). Online portals: Ministry of Finance Tax Portal (tax.nat.gov.tw) and the e-Invoice Integration Service Platform (einvoice.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident establishing a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture in Taiwan must first register the company with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) and obtain a Unified Business Number (UBI). After incorporation, the JV must apply for profit-seeking enterprise income tax registration and Value-Added Business Tax registration at the local National Taxation Bureau under Article 28 of the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act. Required filings include the tax registration application, MOEA business registration certificate or company incorporation certificate, articles of incorporation and JV agreement, identity document of the responsible person, and proof of fixed place of business such as a lease agreement. If the foreign entity is not a local operational JV but sells cross-border electronic services to Taiwan residents without a fixed place of business, it must register for Taiwanese VAT via the Ministry of Finance cross-border e-commerce service platform and receive a foreign-entity VAT registration number; a non-resident without permanent establishment may alternatively obtain a withholding tax account for the Taiwan customer to withhold income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan does not operate a check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election; the Joint Venture is subject to entity-level profit-seeking enterprise income tax and the profits remitted to foreign corporate shareholders are subject to dividend withholding tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax (Taiwan Business Tax; VAT equivalent)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general monetary threshold for a locally incorporated JV; business tax registration is required before any taxable sales commence. Small-scale businesses with monthly taxable turnover below NT$80,000 may be subject to simplified/reduced taxation. A foreign cross-border electronic service provider must register for Taiwan VAT when its annual sales of electronic services to Taiwan resident individuals exceed NT$480,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taxable enterprises must issue Uniform Invoices for all taxable sales. B2B and B2C e-invoices must be uploaded to the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice Integration Service Platform; SaaS/PropTech subscription invoices are issued as cloud e-invoices and transmitted electronically. The platform requires API-based transmission and storage of invoice data for tax authority control, audit matching, and anti-fraud validation; false e-invoices are treated as false Uniform Invoices. Taiwan does not apply a real-time fiscal digital stamping clearance system of the mainland China type.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act, a 0% VAT rate applies to goods exported or delivered outside Taiwan, and to exported services such as cross-border PropTech SaaS when the service is performed for a foreign customer and is not consumed in Taiwan. The foreign-currency consideration must be remitted into Taiwan and supporting documentation must demonstrate the offshore consumption and cross-border nature of the service.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Guan Qu Bao Dan / export customs declaration) authenticated by Taiwan Customs for physical goods
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill for physical export shipments
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the export declaration
Bank Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate or Inward Remittance Water confirming repatriation to Taiwan
Executed service agreement and SaaS usage evidence demonstrating the foreign customer and non-Taiwan consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: National Taxation Bureaus audit the exported goods or services under the export declaration, Uniform Invoice, and FX settlement trail. If the export zero-rating is not substantiated, or the foreign exchange is not received or repatriated within the required period, the zero-rating is reversed and the 5% VAT is assessed retroactively. Under the Business Tax Act and the Tax Collection Act, false invoices or false export documentation can trigger penalties up to five times the evaded tax, prohibition of refunds, and criminal referral for fraudulent tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (中央銀行); foreign-exchange transactions are also governed by the Ministry of Economic Affairs, the Investment Commission, the Foreign Exchange Control Act, the Regulations Governing Foreign Exchange Business, and applicable cross-Strait investment regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Taiwan dollar is generally convertible for bona fide trade, services, and other current-account transactions through authorized foreign-exchange banks. Taiwan generally maintains a liberal current-account regime, subject to transaction reporting, documentary support, anti-money-laundering review, and applicable annual aggregate settlement thresholds. Capital-account transactions, including equity investment, intercompany funding, acquisition of Taiwanese assets, dividends, liquidation proceeds, and certain outbound investments, may require prior approval, registration, or supporting filings. A mainland-China investor or beneficial owner may face additional eligibility, ownership, sector, national-security, and Investment Commission restrictions before capital injection, account opening, dividend remittance, or related-party funding. Profit remittance normally requires audited or approved financial statements, tax clearance or evidence of tax payment, shareholder or board approvals, proof of distributable profits, and evidence that the remittance is not a disguised capital withdrawal or prohibited mainland-China transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan does not generally impose a universal mandatory conversion ratio or automatic surrender requirement for export receipts. Export proceeds may ordinarily be retained in foreign-currency accounts or converted through an authorized foreign-exchange bank, subject to export documentation, invoice and shipping evidence where applicable, bank reporting, and AML review. No general fixed statutory conversion deadline applies solely because proceeds are export receipts; however, the enterprise must comply with applicable trade-settlement, tax, accounting, foreign-exchange reporting, and banking-documentation requirements. Large or unusual settlements may require Central Bank reporting or approval under applicable aggregate annual settlement thresholds. If the operating entity is legally established in mainland China rather than Taiwan, mainland-China SAFE rules, including export-receipt and foreign-exchange settlement rules, would apply instead and this Taiwan assessment would not control.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment collection and treasury support; low for replacing a regulated Taiwanese corporate bank. An offshore electronic-money institution or payment platform cannot ordinarily open a Taiwanese bank account, hold New Taiwan dollars, conduct regulated domestic deposit-taking, or execute foreign-exchange business in Taiwan without the required local authorization. Stripe or comparable providers may support card billing and settlement only subject to merchant underwriting, supported-country rules, settlement-currency limits, beneficial-owner verification, tax documentation, chargeback controls, and Taiwan payment-services requirements. ACH Direct is not a universal Taiwan domestic clearing rail; U.S. ACH generally requires a U.S. account, U.S. collection structure, or an authorized payment intermediary. Customer funds should not be commingled with corporate operating funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening may be available for selected Taiwanese companies and low-risk structures, but it is not guaranteed. Banks may require in-person verification of the legal representative, directors, authorized signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, or mainland-China-connected persons; notarized or legalized corporate documents; Taiwan local-resident contact information; and a video interview. A foreign-invested or mainland-China-linked joint venture should plan for at least one physical onboarding meeting and enhanced review. Remote onboarding does not waive beneficial-owner identification, source-of-funds verification, foreign-investment approval, tax-residency certification, sanctions screening, or transaction-purpose review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mainland-China shareholder, director, controller, funder, or ultimate beneficial owner not clearly disclosed or appearing inconsistent across corporate records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified constitutional documents; complete ownership chart through every natural-person beneficial owner; shareholder registers; passports or identity documents; Taiwan foreign-investment or Investment Commission approvals; mainland-China investment approvals where applicable; director and authorized-signatory resolutions; independent corporate registry extracts; and a written cross-Strait legal-perimeter memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear legal location of the entity because the payload identifies China as sovereign country and Taiwan as jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and registered-office evidence; tax-registration certificate; business-license extract; governing-law memorandum; confirmation of the bank-account jurisdiction; proof of local operating address; and a board resolution expressly identifying whether the account holder is a Taiwan entity or a mainland-China entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection or intercompany funding received from a mainland-China bank, unrelated offshore vehicle, nominee, or third-party payer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed investment or loan agreement; approved capitalization schedule; source-of-funds evidence; originating-bank statements; beneficial-owner declarations; payment-purpose instruction; investment approval or registration; related-party analysis; tax treatment memorandum; and a no-third-party-payment confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PropTech platform appears to provide real-estate brokerage, property management, escrow, rental collection, credit intermediation, or regulated payment services beyond software licensing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product map; customer terms; flow-of-funds diagram; confirmation that the company does not hold client money or make lending decisions; software and SaaS contracts; data-processing policies; legal opinion on licensing; subcontractor list; and segregation controls for customer and corporate funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected transaction activity is inconsistent with the stated low-risk SaaS profile, including high-value property-related payments, cash activity, rapid pass-through transfers, or payments involving restricted jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month cash-flow forecast; customer and supplier concentration report; sample invoices; contracts; payment-purpose taxonomy; expected currencies and corridors; transaction-monitoring rules; sanctions-screening procedure; escalation matrix; and management certification of forecast assumptions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-exchange conversion or remittance lacks a credible commercial purpose, tax support, or documentary trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoices; service agreements; board approvals; tax filings; withholding-tax calculations; dividend resolutions; audited financial statements; proof of distributable earnings; customs or delivery evidence where relevant; and bank payment instructions matching the underlying contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner, senior manager, customer, supplier, or payment counterparty is a sanctioned person, politically exposed person, state-linked entity, or restricted mainland-China party.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current sanctions and PEP screening reports; identity verification; adverse-media search; source-of-wealth evidence; ownership and control analysis; enhanced due-diligence questionnaire; legal restrictions assessment; senior-management approval; and documented transaction rejection or escalation procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore fintech accounts, virtual IBANs, payment aggregators, or personal accounts as the principal treasury channel.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provider licenses and regulatory status; account ownership evidence; safeguarding and segregation terms; settlement-flow diagram; reconciliation policy; chargeback and reserve terms; bank statements; approval matrix; and documented prohibition on personal or nominee accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remote onboarding fails because documents are not authenticated, translated, notarized, legalized, or consistent with bank records.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current registry certificates; certified English or Chinese translations; notarization and legalization or apostille where accepted; specimen signatures; incumbency certificate; power of attorney; tax-residency certificates; and a single controlled corporate-document index.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity capital through a designated capital-injection or investment account at an authorized Taiwan foreign-exchange bank, using the investor's own account and an exact legal-entity name match. The remittance instruction should state the subscription or capital-injection purpose, currency, amount, investor identity, investment approval or registration reference, and beneficiary account. The bank should receive the executed investment agreement, capitalization schedule, corporate resolutions, source-of-funds evidence, ownership chart, and relevant Investment Commission or cross-Strait approvals before or concurrently with settlement. Do not use third-party payers, personal accounts, cash, undisclosed offshore vehicles, or unapproved shareholder loans. The bank should verify sender, beneficial owner, purpose, foreign-exchange reporting classification, sanctions status, and whether the transaction is permissible under Taiwan mainland-China restrictions. After receipt, complete capital registration, accounting recognition, tax reporting, and any required foreign-exchange or investment filings before converting or remitting funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use an authorized Taiwan bank for supplier payments, SaaS infrastructure costs, professional fees, and other bona fide trade or service settlements. SWIFT MT103 or equivalent ISO 20022 customer-credit transfer is suitable for standard cross-border payments; payment instructions should identify the originator, beneficiary, underlying contract or invoice, purpose, currency, intermediary bank, and sanctions-screening data. Use a commercial letter of credit, documentary collection, or bank guarantee where counterparty, shipment, jurisdiction, or performance risk justifies documentary control. For digital services, retain contracts, invoices, acceptance evidence, usage records, tax invoices or withholding-tax analysis, and transfer-pricing support. Reconcile bank statements to the general ledger and invoice register; screen all parties and avoid payment splitting designed to evade reporting thresholds. For customers in mainland China, confirm the applicable cross-Strait trade, payment, data, and counterparty restrictions before accepting or remitting funds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards entered into with an authorized Taiwan foreign-exchange bank for documented commercial exposures, subject to bank credit limits, hedge-purpose evidence, confirmation, valuation, and accounting controls.
Foreign-exchange swaps with an authorized bank for short-term liquidity or currency-mismatch management, subject to applicable bank documentation, suitability, and regulatory requirements.

Currency options or option-based structures offered by an authorized bank, where permitted for the corporate customer and supported by a documented underlying exposure, risk disclosure, and board-approved derivatives policy.

Non-deliverable forwards may be available for selected restricted or non-deliverable currencies through authorized banks, but availability, eligible counterparties, settlement currency, transaction limits, and documentation are bank- and currency-specific; they must not be used to circumvent Taiwan, mainland-China, sanctions, or capital-control rules.

Cross-currency swaps may be used for longer-term funding or recurring currency exposures only with an authorized financial institution, documented hedge accounting, counterparty-credit approval, collateral or margin analysis, and independent valuation.

Speculative foreign-exchange dealing, unlicensed derivatives intermediation, opaque back-to-back structures, and hedges lacking a bona fide business exposure should be prohibited under the treasury policy.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Taiwan profit-seeking enterprises are generally subject to 20% corporate income tax. Qualifying enterprises may claim R&D tax credits, investment tax credits, accelerated depreciation, loss deductions, and incentives under applicable industrial development programs. Undistributed earnings may be subject to an additional 5% tax where applicable. Taiwan generally permits qualifying business losses to be carried forward for 10 years, subject to timely filing, prescribed accounting records, and statutory eligibility conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return filed through Taiwan Ministry of Finance electronic filing systems, including the e-filing portal at tax.nat.gov.tw. The return is generally filed using the applicable profit-seeking enterprise income tax return form and related schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a provisional or interim filing may be required or available under the Income Tax Act depending on the taxpayer's status, accounting period, and filing election.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, the annual return and tax payment are generally due from 1 May through 31 May of the following year. A taxpayer with an approved non-calendar fiscal year generally files within five months after fiscal year-end. Tax authorities may impose separate deadlines for provisional returns, amended returns, requested documentation, and audit responses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the company name, unified business number, registered address, responsible person, accounting period, legal form, tax registration information, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Taiwan entity's own unified business number and tax registration details. Do not substitute the foreign shareholder's tax number unless a specific schedule requests it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the profit or loss according to audited or properly maintained financial accounts before Taiwan income-tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan subsidiary or joint venture reports its Taiwan entity-level accounts. A nonresident shareholder must not consolidate its foreign accounts into the Taiwan company's return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjust accounting profit for nondeductible expenses, exempt income, tax depreciation differences, provisions, fines, entertainment expenses, related-party charges, foreign taxes, and other statutory items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source payments to nonresidents must be reconciled with withholding certificates, contractual support, beneficial-owner evidence, and any treaty or cross-strait relief documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report SaaS subscriptions, platform fees, property-management technology fees, implementation charges, data services, advertising revenue, and other Taiwan taxable business receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate revenue based on contractual rights, functions performed, customer location, service performance, and applicable Taiwan sourcing rules. Do not use payment-processor location alone to determine source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cost of goods sold and operating expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report deductible payroll, cloud hosting, software development, depreciation, rent, marketing, professional fees, commissions, and other operating expenses, subject to substantiation and business-purpose requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign service providers require evidence of services, place of performance, invoice support, withholding analysis, and transfer-pricing support where the provider is related.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose controlled transactions involving goods, services, royalties, financing, guarantees, cost allocations, restructuring, and other dealings with related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the foreign parent, affiliates, ultimate beneficial owners, transaction amounts, currencies, terms, and applicable withholding. Reconcile all schedules to the general ledger and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report any voluntary or audit-related adjustment required to bring controlled transactions to an arm's-length result under Taiwan transfer-pricing rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent cannot create a Taiwan deduction merely through an intercompany debit. The Taiwan entity must demonstrate benefit received, arm's-length pricing, actual performance, and consistency with the functional analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate taxable income after statutory adjustments, permitted deductions, approved incentives, and eligible loss utilization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply only losses and incentives legally attributable to the Taiwan taxpayer. Foreign shareholder losses and foreign group tax attributes are not available to the Taiwan entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 20% corporate income tax rate, permitted investment or R&D credits, foreign tax credits where available, withholding credits, and prior payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain Taiwan withholding certificates and foreign tax evidence. Foreign tax credits are subject to statutory limitation and generally cannot exceed the Taiwan tax attributable to the relevant foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determine whether retained post-tax earnings are subject to the additional 5% undistributed earnings tax and report permitted distributions or capital reinvestment exclusions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends paid to foreign shareholders do not eliminate the Taiwan company's separate undistributed earnings tax exposure for the relevant year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile tax withheld on salaries, professional fees, rent, royalties, interest, dividends, and payments to nonresident enterprises against withholding filings and payment receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Taiwan payer generally bears the operational responsibility for withholding, payment, certificates, and filing. Gross-up clauses may increase the Taiwan taxable and withholding base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submit financial statements, tax reconciliation schedules, related-party disclosures, supporting ledgers, withholding evidence, incentive applications, and other documents required by the filing method or tax authority.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-language documents may require Chinese translations, notarization, legalization, or tax-residency evidence depending on the requested relief and administrative practice.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing generally triggers a surcharge based on tax payable, with statutory minimum and maximum amounts. Failure to file may trigger a higher surcharge and assessment by the tax authority. Late payment generally attracts statutory interest, commonly calculated by month or part of a month under the Tax Collection Act, and may lead to compulsory collection, attachment, restrictions on departure, and director or responsible-person measures where legally available. Understatement, omitted income, unsupported deductions, or false documents may trigger additional tax, penalties, and criminal investigation.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed by a Taiwan company to a nonresident shareholder, subject to applicable exemptions, special rules, and treaty or cross-strait relief.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, the Taiwan payer should obtain evidence of the recipient's tax residence, beneficial ownership, legal status, ownership percentage, holding period, and entitlement to relief. The payer should apply to the competent Taiwan tax authority for advance approval where required, or withhold at the domestic rate and seek a refund where the applicable administrative procedure requires post-payment relief. Taiwan does not have a conventional income tax treaty with Mainland China; transactions involving Mainland Chinese investors may be governed by cross-strait regulations, investment approvals, and special tax rules rather than an ordinary DTA. A Taiwan tax residency certificate is generally issued by the competent tax authority upon application and does not by itself establish treaty entitlement in another jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Taiwan withholding is generally 20% on Taiwan-source royalties and interest paid to nonresident enterprises, subject to statutory exceptions, reduced rates, exemptions, or approved treaty relief. Treaty rates vary by treaty and payment category. Payments for software, know-how, technical services, cloud services, equipment use, and mixed contracts require separate characterization; a payment described as a service fee may be recharacterized as a royalty or Taiwan-source service income. Taiwan-source interest and royalties paid to Mainland Chinese recipients may be subject to special cross-strait rules and should not be assumed to qualify for ordinary treaty rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Taiwan generally requires transfer-pricing disclosure and supporting documentation for controlled transactions. A taxpayer may qualify for simplified documentation only where applicable revenue and controlled-transaction thresholds are not exceeded; commonly relevant thresholds include annual revenue below NTD 300,000,000 and aggregate controlled transactions below NTD 200,000,000, subject to transaction-specific exceptions. A Local File is generally required when the applicable exemption is unavailable. A Master File is generally relevant where the multinational enterprise group's annual consolidated revenue reaches at least NTD 27,000,000,000 and the Taiwan entity has relevant controlled transactions. Country-by-Country Reporting generally applies at the same NTD 27,000,000,000 consolidated-revenue threshold, subject to reporting-entity and filing rules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not operate a single UAE-style standalone Economic Substance Regulations regime. Substance is enforced through transfer-pricing rules, anti-avoidance provisions, beneficial-ownership analysis, business-purpose requirements, controlled-foreign-company rules, place-of-effective-management considerations, source rules, and deductibility requirements. A Taiwan entity claiming deductions for related-party SaaS development, management, licensing, financing, or platform support must demonstrate personnel, decision-making, assets, risk control, actual performance, commercial benefit, and arm's-length pricing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing Taiwan revenue, issuing false invoices, omitting platform income, using sham expenses, maintaining parallel books, manipulating related-party prices, or deliberately understating taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax, statutory administrative penalties, interest, compulsory collection, and criminal exposure under the Income Tax Act and related criminal laws. Serious tax evasion may result in imprisonment of the responsible person and substantial fines, with the exact sanction depending on conduct, tax amount, intent, and prosecution provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons and directors may face criminal prosecution, personal fines, civil liability for losses, restitution of unpaid taxes, asset preservation, restrictions on departure, and enforcement against personal assets where statutory conditions are met. Limited liability does not protect intentional personal misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating or accepting fictitious invoices, backdating contracts, fabricating cloud-service records, recording non-existent development work, falsifying payroll, or using sham intercompany charges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, denial of deductions or credits, invoice-related penalties, fines, and potential criminal liability for document fraud, tax fraud, or commercial-accounting violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, responsible persons, finance officers, and cooperating advisers may be jointly exposed to criminal investigation, civil restitution, personal fines, asset seizure, and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length royalties, management fees, cost allocations, financing charges, guarantees, or development charges to shift Taiwan profit to a foreign shareholder without evidence of benefit or substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income adjustment to an arm's-length result, denial of deductions, additional corporate income tax, withholding tax assessment, interest, penalties, and possible anti-avoidance reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability for tax losses and breach of fiduciary duties. Deliberate false documentation or collusion may create criminal exposure for the responsible person and participating officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper dividend, interest, royalty, or service payment withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold, applying an unsupported treaty rate, misclassifying royalties as services, grossing up without reporting the gross amount, or remitting funds before obtaining required documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid withholding tax from the Taiwan payer, interest, withholding penalties, filing penalties, and possible disallowance of the related deduction. The payer may remain liable even where the foreign recipient received the full net payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible person and withholding officers may face administrative and civil liability. Deliberate concealment or false certificates may result in criminal proceedings and restrictions on departure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful Mainland Chinese investment or nominee ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Allowing an undisclosed Mainland Chinese investor to control or fund the Taiwan joint venture through nominees, offshore intermediaries, layered shareholding, or unapproved beneficial ownership arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Investment approval violations may lead to fines, orders to dispose of shares, cancellation or revocation of approvals, restrictions on operations, confiscation or corrective measures, and penalties under Taiwan regulations governing Mainland-area investment and cross-strait economic relations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible persons may face personal fines, disqualification or removal consequences, civil damages, criminal exposure for false filings, asset restrictions, and possible travel restrictions. Foreign shareholders may also face enforcement against Taiwan-located assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Taiwan company with no genuine personnel, decision-making, systems, customer activity, or operational risk while booking artificial income or deductions for a foreign group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of deductions, transfer-pricing adjustments, source recharacterization, withholding assessments, anti-avoidance reassessment, interest, penalties, and possible revocation or regulatory action where registration or business activity is fictitious.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for unpaid taxes, creditor losses, and misleading filings. Intentional sham arrangements can create criminal exposure, asset preservation, and departure restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering and suspicious payment routing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing customer receipts through undisclosed accounts, using nominee shareholders, structuring transfers, concealing beneficial owners, mixing company and personal funds, or transferring unexplained funds through offshore payment processors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reporting, customer-identification, recordkeeping, account-freezing, administrative, and criminal sanctions under Taiwan anti-money-laundering laws. Serious money-laundering conduct may carry imprisonment and substantial fines, with penalties depending on amount, predicate offense, and intent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, responsible persons, compliance officers, and beneficial owners may face criminal liability, confiscation, restitution, asset freezing, travel restrictions, and imprisonment. Corporate limited liability does not shield knowing participants.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating regulated property-management, brokerage, payment, data, telecommunications, or financial activities without required approval, or describing a SaaS service inaccurately to avoid licensing or tax obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory fines, cease-and-desist orders, suspension or revocation of registrations, customer refunds, tax reassessment, and criminal penalties where the relevant sector law provides them.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may face personal administrative fines, civil claims, criminal prosecution for unauthorized operations, and restrictions on departure in connection with unpaid penalties or criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing tenant, landlord, identity, credit, location, or payment data without lawful basis, adequate security, required notices, consent, retention controls, or cross-border transfer governance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, corrective orders, suspension of data processing, customer compensation, cybersecurity sanctions, and potential criminal liability for unlawful disclosure or misuse of personal data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible persons may face civil damages, administrative sanctions, and criminal exposure for intentional or grossly negligent misuse or disclosure of protected information.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to maintain books, records, and audit trail
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Destroying accounting records, failing to preserve electronic logs, omitting related-party agreements, using unsupported cash payments, or failing to reconcile Stripe, ACH, bank, invoice, and general-ledger data.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Estimated assessment, denial of deductions, penalties, audit escalation, withholding reassessment, and possible criminal exposure if records are intentionally destroyed or falsified.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The responsible person and directors may be liable for resulting tax losses, creditor claims, and obstruction-related sanctions. Personal asset enforcement and departure restrictions may apply under tax collection or criminal procedures.
